    Proposition 10.1(1) in all degrees and 10.1(3): the presentation of E₄ #

    prop:fixed-integral-companion (integral-deformations.tex): (1) the Hom modules of E₄ are free over 𝒪 and E₄/2E₄ = C⁽²⁾; "the same two reductions exclude negative-degree Hom spaces"; (3) "E₄ has a quadratic scalar mesh presentation with unit coefficients reducing to the all-one presentation of C⁽²⁾".

    • Evaluation over 𝔽₂ is full (rs_surj, from Proposition 2.10's evMap_surjective) and faithful (rs_inj); a graded map of degree d is the evaluation of a morphism of degree d, and there are none in negative degrees (exists_rs_of_homD, homD_eq_bot_of_neg).
    • The graded Hom modules of the lifts vanish in negative degrees (homD'_eq_bot_of_neg), so (1) holds in every degree (integralHomFree_all).
    • Path evaluation 𝒪Q → E₄ along the lifted arrows (evO) is onto the graded maps of every degree, by length-homogeneous path combinations (evO_surj), and its kernel is exactly the ideal of the unit mesh relations (evO_eq_zero_iff): this is the presentation (3).

    def MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.MeshWalk.Prop101Stmt {V : Type} [Quiver V] [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] {Q : TranslationQuiver V} [(x : V) → Fintype ((y : V) × (y ⟶ x))] {c : MeshCoefficients (ZMod 2) Q} {L : CatAlg.LocalFamily (meshFam Q c)} {D : CatAlg.MeshData (meshFam Q c) L} [hfd : ∀ (x y : V), FiniteDimensional (ZMod 2) (meshFam Q c x ⟶ meshFam Q c y)] {R : Type} [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R] {P : RaySys.Mult D.PV R} (T : TabIso D P) :
    Prop

    The statement of Proposition 10.1 (prop:fixed-integral-companion) for the table T: the modules M_X⁽²⁾ lift to graded 𝒪P-modules free over 𝒪 with degree-one arrow lifts (WData), and their graded Hom category E₄ satisfies (1) its Hom modules are free over 𝒪 in every degree, with E₄/2E₄ the graded Homs of the modules of C⁽²⁾, which are the morphisms of C⁽²⁾ of the same degree; (2) at projective labels the lifts are ẽ_s𝒪P, through the generator w_s; (3) E₄ is presented by the quadratic mesh relations with unit coefficients u reducing to the all-one coefficients c: path evaluation is onto every graded Hom module (by paths of the same length) and its kernel is the ideal of the u-mesh relations.
